# Two modality descriptors, two different recalls

*Generated by `scripts/atlas_descriptor_recall.py`. Every figure is recomputed.*

Over the 13,346 census articles indexed `Ferroptosis`, measured with one text rule applied identically to both arms:

| arm | descriptor | text says so | descriptor | both | recall | precision |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| PDT | `Photochemotherapy` | 182 | 152 | 146 | **80.2%** | 96.1% |
| SDT | `Ultrasonic Therapy` | 63 | 32 | 29 | **46.0%** | 90.6% |

The two descriptors are comparably **precise** and differ by a factor of **1.74** in **recall**.

## What that does to the ratio the manuscript states

| how the two are counted | ratio |
|---|--:|
| by descriptor (what `manuscript-vs-census.md` reports) | **4.75:1** |
| by one text rule applied to both | **2.89:1** |
| as the manuscript states it | 2.93:1 |

So the census does not exceed the manuscript by 62%. Measured symmetrically it **reproduces** the manuscript's ratio to within 1.4%.

That is a stronger result for the manuscript than the one being withdrawn: an independent instrument over the whole indexed cancer literature lands on the figure it published. What does not survive is the claim that the manuscript **understated** its own case, which rested on comparing two descriptors that do not capture their concepts equally well.

## Why the existing symmetry check did not catch this

`manuscript-vs-census.md` does test for asymmetry and concludes "the gap is 3.3 points, so the over-estimation is symmetric". That is a test of **precision** -- what share of each descriptor's records are on-modality -- and precision genuinely is symmetric. Recall was never measured, and that is where the asymmetry is.

The same document varies four alternative descriptor sets and reports that every variant exceeds the manuscript's ratio. Every variant is built from descriptors, so all four inherit the same recall gap. A sensitivity analysis over descriptor sets cannot detect a descriptor-versus-text recall problem.

## The caveat this inverts

Five files state that `Ultrasonic Therapy` is broader than sonodynamic therapy, so the count is an OVER-estimate and ratios against it are LOWER bounds. The breadth is real and small: precision 90.6%, i.e. 3 of 32 records. Recall is 46.0%, which is far larger and runs the other way, so the count is an **under**-estimate and ratios against it are **upper** bounds.

The records carrying the descriptor whose text does not say sonodynamic -- the whole of the over-count -- are:

* 34646381 — Ultrasound (US)-activated redox dyshomeostasis therapy reinforced by immunogenic cell death (ICD) through a mi
* 39987131 — Engineering nanozyme immunomodulator with magnetic targeting effect for cascade-enzyodynamic and ultrasound-re
* 40557564 — An Electronegativity-Modulated Piezoelectric Metal-Organic Framework for Tumor Piezocatalytic Ferroptosis.

## Why the two descriptors differ, which is its own finding

Photodynamic therapy has a dedicated MeSH descriptor. Sonodynamic therapy has none, and is indexed under a broader physical-modality term when it is indexed at all. That is the mechanism `analysis/atlas-untagged-partner.md` measured inside this project's own taxonomy -- a modality with no name of its own is recorded under someone else's -- appearing again one layer up, in MeSH.

## What this does not claim

* Not that the manuscript is wrong. Its ratio is reproduced almost exactly by an independent instrument.
* Not that the text rule is ground truth. It has errors in both directions. The point is that it is applied IDENTICALLY to both arms, which the descriptor comparison is not.
* Not that either descriptor is a bad descriptor. They are comparably precise; they are applied at different rates.
